comparison: Both support the cryo-EM structural findings (C42-C48). OpenEval emphasizes resolution values and structural features with appropriate documentation. Peer review focuses on validation by concurrent publications (C113-C114) and acknowledges this as confirmatory work. Both treat structural claims as well-supported.

Both strongly support the chromatin-binding interface claims (C60-C67). OpenEval highlights structural data, mutagenesis validation, and sequence conservation. Peer review accepts these findings as revealing substrate specificity mechanisms without critique. Complete agreement on the quality and interpretation of this evidence.

Both support DNA unwrapping claims (C49-C56). OpenEval emphasizes cryo-EM data and MD simulations showing SIRT6-induced conformational changes. Peer review accepts the DNA unwinding mechanism without critique and treats it as part of the visualization of SIRT6 on its native target. Full agreement.

Both support conformational heterogeneity claims (C13, C57-C59). OpenEval validates findings through cryoDRGN analysis and structural comparisons. Peer review emphasizes this as a novel contribution providing 'new insights into potential dynamics' and structural flexibility. Both treat this as a key advance beyond concurrent work.

Perfect agreement on DNA-binding residue claims (C68, C70-C71). Both support structural observations and mutagenesis validation. OpenEval notes clear structural interactions and functional validation. Peer review accepts findings as part of overall characterization without critique. Complete concordance.

Both support MD simulation findings about H3 tail positioning (C14-C15, C83-C89). OpenEval validates the scanning mechanism as reasonable inference from structural data. Peer review explicitly supports MD analysis as explaining substrate specificity. Both treat mechanistic model as key contribution with overlapping claims (C80-C82, C97-C100).

Both support novel H3K27Ac deacetylation findings (C90-C94, C106-C107). OpenEval emphasizes MD predictions and experimental validation with statistical significance. Peer review highlights this as a novel finding that clarifies SIRT6 activity. Complete agreement on the importance and validation of alternative tail pathways.

Both support H2A.Z binding preference claims (C78-C79). OpenEval notes statistically significant gel-shift data but considers gene expression connection speculative. Peer review accepts findings and speculation without critique. Agreement on experimental data quality, with speculation appropriately qualified.

Divergent evaluations of H2A K119 ubiquitination claims (C76-C77). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C76 is structurally supported but C77 is purely speculative without experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the speculation as reasonable. OpenEval requires additional experiments; peer review does not.

Divergent evaluations of helix α13 flexibility claims (C74-C75). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, supporting C74 structurally but noting C75 is explicitly speculative without validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic speculation as reasonable inference. OpenEval distinguishes observation from speculation more strictly.

Both support background claims (C1-C8) as well-established facts appropriately cited from prior work. OpenEval notes these provide essential context. Peer review treats them as accepted knowledge framing the significance. Complete agreement that these foundational statements are accurate.

Both support extensive background claims (C16-C41). OpenEval validates these as accurately represented and properly attributed context from introduction. Peer review accepts them as established background providing context for new findings. Full concordance on the quality of literature review.

Both support mechanistic synthesis claims (C95-C100, C97-C100 overlap). OpenEval validates these as well-supported inferences from structural data, MD simulations, and mutagenesis. Peer review accepts the mechanistic model as explaining substrate specificity. Agreement on the logical integration of evidence.

Both support PRC1 comparison claims (C101-C103). OpenEval notes reasonable comparison highlighting similarities and differences supported by structural data. Peer review accepts this as appropriate scholarly discussion contextualizing SIRT6's unique features. Complete agreement.

OpenEval supports mechanistic synthesis claims (C104-C105) integrating prior work with current findings. These overlap with peer R12's background claims (C95-C96 shared). Both treat the integration of prior biochemical data with new structural findings as well-supported and satisfying.

Both support H3K27 deacetylation claims (C106-C107 overlap) and K56 discussion (C108-C109). OpenEval validates MD and experimental evidence while noting C109 is appropriately qualified speculation. Peer review accepts the H3K27Ac finding as novel. Agreement on validated claims; OpenEval more explicit about speculative elements.

Divergent evaluations of predictions about other enzymes (C110-C112). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but speculative predictions without experimental evidence, representing testable hypotheses rather than supported conclusions. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting them as appropriate scholarly speculation. OpenEval applies stricter evidence standard.

Both support acknowledgment of concurrent work (C113-C114). OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment validating reproducibility of key findings. Peer review emphasizes this manuscript confirms and complements previous findings. Complete agreement on the confirmatory nature and appropriate citation.

Both support background citations (C69, C72-C73). OpenEval validates these as established findings providing context for structure interpretation. Peer review treats them as accepted knowledge. Complete agreement that prior work is accurately represented.

Both support H3 tail conformation background (C80-C82). OpenEval notes these cite well-established NMR and MD studies providing basis for current analysis. Peer review accepts these as foundation for MD analysis explaining substrate specificity. Complete agreement on the validity of this foundation.
